1. Core Clinical Tension: A 34-year-old woman presented with intractable constipation, profound 10-kg weight loss, and a massive 28-week-sized multilocular pelvic mass densely adherent to reproductive organs with severe anemia (Hb 7 g/dL), raising high suspicion for advanced ovarian cystadenocarcinoma or gastrointestinal malignancy.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission presentation with pelvic examination showing a 28-week-sized cystic mass, baseline labs showing microcytic anemia of 7 g/dL, pelvic ultrasound and pelvic CT demonstrating extensive multicystic lesions involving the uterus and adnexa, prior to exploratory laparotomy and histopathology.
3. Differential Distinctions: Advanced ovarian or pelvic malignancy was ruled out by absence of distant metastasis and benign parasitic histology on excision; colorectal neoplasia was excluded by normal colonoscopy; microscopic confirmation of Echinococcus granulosus scolices and laminated cuticular membrane established pelvic hydatid disease.
case_prompt: A 34-year-old woman (gravida 3, para 3) presented with a 4-month history of lower abdominal pain, anorexia, progressive severe constipation, and an unintentional weight loss of more than 10 kg. She reported no fever, nausea, or vomiting. She had previously undergone an outpatient diagnostic colonoscopy for gastrointestinal symptoms, which revealed normal colonic mucosa without luminal lesions. On physical examination, the abdomen was distended by a non-tender, smooth, uniformly cystic mass palpated in the lower abdomen and pelvis corresponding in size to a 28-week gravid uterus. Speculum examination was unremarkable. Baseline laboratory evaluation demonstrated microcytic anemia with a hemoglobin level of 7.0 g/dL, with a normal total leukocyte count. Blood glucose, blood urea nitrogen, serum creatinine, liver transaminases, and urinalysis were normal; fecal occult blood testing and a serum pregnancy test were negative. Plain chest radiography was normal. Transabdominal pelvic ultrasonography demonstrated multiple anechoic cystic masses occupying the pelvis and abutting the uterus. Pelvic computed tomography revealed multiple cystic space-occupying lesions involving the uterus, broad ligament, and bilateral adnexa.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Advanced gynecologic / pelvic malignancy (e.g., ovarian cystadenocarcinoma)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: A massive 28-week-sized pelvic mass associated with severe anemia (Hb 7 g/dL) and rapid 10-kg weight loss strongly simulated ovarian or peritoneal malignancy; however, abdominal/chest CT and bone scintigraphy showed no metastasis, and surgical pathology demonstrated non-neoplastic parasitic cyst membranes.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The patient underwent an exploratory laparotomy under general anesthesia for further diagnosis of the cystic mass, and ruling out of the genitourinary malignancy. Preoperative laboratory evaluation including HIV antibody, VDRL test, HBS antigen, and HCV antibody assay were normal. Additionally, whole body bone scan, chest and abdominal CT scan were also performed that revealed unremarkable results.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Severe gastrointestinal malignancy or extrinsic colonic obstruction
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Severe intractable constipation and profound weight loss suggested colonic obstruction from primary colorectal cancer; however, diagnostic colonoscopy demonstrated completely normal mucosa and lumen, confirming that bowel symptoms were due to extrinsic compression by pelvic cysts.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: As the patient had severe constipation and other gastrointestinal symptoms, colonoscopy had been carried out in another center with normal findings.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Pelvic endometriosis or benign ovarian cystadenoma
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Endometriomas or simple cystadenomas rarely present as massive, densely adherent multilocular cysts filling the broad ligament and adnexa with marked anemia and constitutional wasting, and histology revealed characteristic scolices rather than endometrial or serous/mucinous epithelium.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: At the operation, numerous ovarian and paraovarian cystic masses densely adhered to the uterus, to the pelvic side wall, and to the fallopian tubes were demonstrated.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Exploratory laparotomy with excision of pelvic and adnexal cystic lesions demonstrated characteristic hydatid cysts, confirmed on microscopic examination by the presence of Echinococcus granulosus scolices and adjacent laminated cuticular membranes.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Microscopic examination disclosed the scolices of Echinococcus granulosis with adjacent laminated membrane and confirmed the diagnosis (Figure 2).

editor_comments: Primary pelvic hydatidosis masquerading as an advanced gynecological malignancy with cachexia, constipation, and severe anemia.
